objective: Port netty-codec-http 4.2.19.Final (io.netty.handler.codec.http with its cookie, cors, multipart and websocketx packages, io.netty.handler.codec.rtsp and io.netty.handler.codec.spdy) to Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Http with the original names, structure, comments and tests.

ownerDecisions: Project, folder and assembly names are the namespace root of the module (owner decision 2026-11-19, see docs/codec-base-porting.md): each codec module takes the namespace of its main package, and the tests use <project>.Tests like the other test projects.

Owner decisions 2026-11-19 for the codec modules that only need codec-base: one project per Maven module; codec-socks is Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Socks (its Maven and JPMS name) and holds the socks and socksx namespaces; haproxy is HAProxy (the casing of the Java types in that package); socksx, v4 and v5 are Socksx, V4 and V5.

Owner decisions 2026-11-24 for codec-http: one project Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Http for the Maven module; namespaces Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Http, .Http.Cookie, .Http.Cors, .Http.Multipart, .Http.WebSocketx, .Http.WebSocketx.Extensions and .Http.WebSocketx.Extensions.Compression (websocketx takes the casing of its Java types, as ipfilter became IpFilter), Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Rtsp and Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Spdy, in the folders Cookie/, Cors/, Multipart/, WebSocketx/, Rtsp/ and Spdy/ (as codec-socks keeps Socksx/); the zlib preset dictionary that SPDY header blocks need is implemented on the BCL streams in the java.util.zip.Deflater/Inflater stand-ins of codec-compression (a stored block primes the inflater, the deflater compresses the dictionary and keeps only what follows its sync flush; measured interoperable with the reference zlib), which codec-http uses through InternalsVisibleTo.

review.scope: CharSequence is ICharSequence and String is string; both Java overloads are kept, and the String values compared or stored as CharSequence are wrapped in the Common StringCharSequence because a C# string is not an ICharSequence; Integer/Short/Long results are int?/short?/long?; Iterable<?> is IEnumerable<object> (a value-type IEnumerable binds to the Object overload); Map.Entry and Iterator are the codec-base IEntry and IIterator (docs/codec-base-porting.md, Headers). The wrapped DefaultHeaders<CharSequence, CharSequence, ?> uses a wildcard, which C# cannot express: the headers are a DefaultHeaders<ICharSequence, ICharSequence, HeadersImpl>, where HeadersImpl is a public abstract nested class (CLR-only) that the default headers (DefaultHeadersImpl in Java, the private nested DefaultImpl) and CombinedHttpHeadersImpl derive from. copy() is new DefaultHttpHeaders(headers.copy()) as in Java: DefaultHeaders.Copy() creates a DefaultHeaders<K, V, T> of its exact type, which is not a HeadersImpl and whose this-returning members return null instead of failing, as Java's unchecked (T) this fails only where the result is used (codec-base DefaultHeaders.ThisT, 2026-11-24; the former HeadersImpl.Copy() override with a DefaultImpl is gone); DefaultHttpHeaders ignores those results, and, as in Java, the copy of combined headers is a plain DefaultHeaders (measured: a copy of DefaultHttpHeaders takes Add/Set chains, and a copy of combined headers keeps the combined value "1,2" and adds a later value separately). unwrap() returns IHeaders<ICharSequence, ICharSequence, HeadersImpl>; for a copy its this-returning results are null where Java returns the object. Public class over HttpContentEncoder. CompressionOptions is codec-compression's ICompressionOptions (CompressionOptions... is params ICompressionOptions[]) and BrotliOptions/GzipOptions/DeflateOptions/SnappyOptions, StandardCompressionOptions, BrotliEncoder, SnappyFrameEncoder, ZlibCodecFactory and ZlibWrapper are the codec-compression ports. Zstandard comes from zstd-jni (com.github.luben.zstd, a JNI binding). System.IO.Compression gains ZstandardStream/ZstandardEncoder/ZstandardDecoder only in .NET 11 (its API page lists net-11.0 only), and the owner kept the solution on .NET 10 and decided on 2026-11-23 not to port the Zstd family (docs/codec-compression-porting.md), so Zstd, ZstdOptions, ZstdEncoder and ZstdDecoder have no C# type. The CLR code behaves as Java does when Zstd.isAvailable() is false (zstd-jni absent from the class path). StandardCompressionOptions.zstd() is never a default option, no option can select zstd and the zstd case of createEncoderFor throws "Zstd not configured"; the zstdOptions field stays as an always-null ICompressionOptions so that determineEncoding keeps its Java shape. brotli4j is not ported either: Brotli.IsAvailable() is always true (the BCL BrotliEncoder) and BrotliOptions.parameters(), which returns the brotli4j Encoder.Parameters, is not ported, so the BrotliEncoder is created from the BrotliOptions themselves (the codec-compression BrotliEncoder(BrotliOptions) constructor). The @Deprecated constructors HttpContentCompressor(int), (int, int, int) and (int, int, int, int), the protected determineWrapper(String) and the private defaultCompressionOptions(GzipOptions, DeflateOptions) have no @deprecated text naming a replacement, so they are ported with [Obsolete] (owner decision 2026-11-16); they still validate the levels with checkInRange, but ZlibCodecFactory.NewZlibEncoder throws NotSupportedException for a window size or memory level other than 15/8, which need the not-ported jzlib (docs/codec-compression-porting.md, ZlibCodecFactory). ZlibWrapper is a C# enum (a value type), so DetermineWrapper returns ZlibWrapper?, where Java returns a null reference. The protected determineEncoding is protected virtual DetermineEncoding (the Java method is overridable). The static initializer is the static constructor. Float.parseFloat is float.Parse with NumberStyles.Float and the invariant culture after HttpUtil.TrimJava (Java trims as String.trim); an invalid q-value is the FormatException of the NumberFormatException and takes the catch branch (q = 0.0f). Java's grammar (Double.valueOf) also accepts a trailing f/F/d/D suffix and hexadecimal floats, which float.Parse rejects, so such a q-value counts as 0.0f in the CLR; an overflowing value is infinity in both ("In .NET Core 3.0 and later, values that are too large to represent are rounded to PositiveInfinity or NegativeInfinity"). String.contains is the ordinal string.Contains and the switch on the encoding string is a C# string switch. IllegalStateException is InvalidOperationException and IllegalArgumentException is ArgumentException. EmbeddedChannel.builder() is new EmbeddedChannel.Builder() with ChannelId/HasDisconnect/Config/Handlers/Build.

Public abstract extension point over the codec-base MessageToMessageDecoder<IHttpObject>; the implicit Java constructor is the public parameterless constructor passing typeof(IHttpObject) (docs/codec-base-porting.md, Type matching). review.scope: Public class over HttpContentDecoder with the constructors HttpContentDecompressor(int maxAllocation) and (bool strict, int maxAllocation) and the protected override NewContentDecoder(string). gzip/x-gzip, deflate/x-deflate (ZLIB when strict, ZLIB_OR_NONE otherwise), br and snappy build an EmbeddedChannel with new EmbeddedChannel.Builder() and the codec-compression decoders (ZlibCodecFactory.NewZlibDecoder, BrotliDecoder.NewDecoderWithMaxAllocation, SnappyFrameDecoder); Brotli.IsAvailable() is always true (the BCL BrotliDecoder). Zstandard comes from zstd-jni (com.github.luben.zstd, a JNI binding). System.IO.Compression gains ZstandardStream/ZstandardEncoder/ZstandardDecoder only in .NET 11 (its API page lists net-11.0 only), and the owner kept the solution on .NET 10 and decided on 2026-11-23 not to port the Zstd family (docs/codec-compression-porting.md), so Zstd, ZstdOptions, ZstdEncoder and ZstdDecoder have no C# type. The "Zstd.isAvailable() && ZSTD" branch is left out, so a "zstd" Content-Encoding is passed through undecoded (null), as in Java without zstd-jni. AsciiString.contentEqualsIgnoreCase(CharSequence) takes the String encoding wrapped in StringCharSequence. The two @Deprecated constructors whose @deprecated texts name HttpContentDecompressor(int) and HttpContentDecompressor(boolean, int) are not ported (owner decision 2026-11-16).

Public abstract extension point over the codec-base MessageToMessageCodec<IHttpRequest, IHttpObject>; super(HttpRequest.class, HttpObject.class) is base(typeof(IHttpRequest), typeof(IHttpObject)) (docs/codec-base-porting.md, Type matching). The Java public/protected members keep their Java names: DEFAULT_MAX_PIPELINE_DEPTH (public const), the two constructors, the overrides AcceptOutboundMessage/Decode/Encode/HandlerRemoved/ChannelInactive, the protected abstract BeginEncode(IHttpResponse, string) and the public static final nested class Result (a public sealed nested class with the public constructor and the TargetContentEncoding()/ContentEncoder() accessor methods). The private state enum and helpers keep their names. The Accept-Encoding queue (ArrayDeque<CharSequence>) is Queue<string>: the queued values are the String values of the request headers or the String constants IDENTITY, ZERO_LENGTH_HEAD and ZERO_LENGTH_CONNECT, so isPassthru keeps Java's reference comparison of those constants with ReferenceEquals; poll() is TryDequeue (null when empty) and StringUtil.join(",", list) is string.Join. The AWAIT_HEADERS switch section falls through into AWAIT_CONTENT after its try/finally; C# switch sections cannot fall through, so a goto case follows the finally block. ByteBufHolder is IByteBufHolder (Content property), EmbeddedChannel.readOutbound() is ReadOutbound<ByteBuf>(), IllegalStateException is InvalidOperationException, catch (Throwable) is catch (Exception) and assert is Debug.Assert. In the exception messages Class.getName()/getSimpleName() are Type.FullName/Type.Name of the C# interfaces (IHttpResponse, IHttpContent), and the pipeline depth prints with the invariant culture.

Cloneable is ICloneable: clone() returns HttpDecoderConfig through MemberwiseClone() (Object.clone()'s shallow copy) and ICloneable.Clone() is explicit; the CloneNotSupportedException/AssertionError branch cannot occur; HttpHeadersFactory is IHttpHeadersFactory.

review.scope: ByteToMessageDecoder subclass with the Java state machine: fall-through sections end with goto case and a try block that falls through jumps after it; Runnable is Action and the anonymous Runnables/ByteProcessor are lambdas; AtomicBoolean is the Common AtomicBoolean (lazySet is Set); array()/arrayOffset() of the heap scratch buffer are the array segment of the line's readable memory (LineArray, copied when not array-backed; docs/buffer-porting.md, Array extraction). Java byte sign: SP_LENIENT_BYTES, LATIN_WHITESPACE and ISO_CONTROL_OR_WHITESPACE are indexed by the signed byte + 128, so lookups read the octet as sbyte; Character.isWhitespace/isISOControl of a byte widen the signed value (0x80-0xFF are neither) and the Java loops stop before 0x7F; exception texts print the signed octet. new String(bytes, 0, start, len) is Encoding.Latin1.GetString; trim() is HttpUtil.TrimJava; Long.parseLong is HttpUtil.ParseLong. The two static initializers are one static constructor. The obsolete validateHeaders field is assigned under #pragma warning disable CS0618 (javac does not warn inside the same class, JLS 9.6.4.6). The inner LineParser reads the decoder's state through the decoder it receives; HeaderParser.parse reads this.size before its local size (CS0841). ChannelFutureListener.CLOSE/CLOSE_ON_FAILURE are continuations of the write Task on Common's CLR-only EventExecutorTaskScheduler over ctx.Executor (owner decision 2026-11-24; the scheduler of handler's IdleStateHandler too, docs/handler-porting.md, Listener timing): the Transport completes its operation Tasks with RunContinuationsAsynchronously (src/Netty.NET.Transport/Channels/AbstractChannel.cs), so a continuation on TaskScheduler.Default ran later on a thread-pool thread and HttpServerKeepAliveHandlerTest saw the channel still open (43 of 49 cases failed, measured), while Java's DefaultPromise notifies the listener at once when the write completes on the event loop; the scheduler runs the continuation at once on the event loop (EmbeddedEventLoop.InEventLoop is always true, src/Netty.NET.Transport/Channels/Embedded/EmbeddedEventLoop.cs) and otherwise hands it to Execute.

Public class over the Transport ChannelDuplexHandler with the Java fields and private helpers. channelRead is the ChannelRead override; write(ctx, msg, promise) is the Task-returning WriteAsync override (the Task replaces the promise, docs/codec-base-porting.md, Outbound operations). promise.unvoid().addListener(ChannelFutureListener.CLOSE) before super.write: Java closes the channel when the write completes or fails, also when writing throws (the pipeline then fails the promise); the port closes it from a continuation of the returned Task, or before rethrowing a synchronous exception of base.WriteAsync; unvoid() has no counterpart because there is no void promise. ChannelFutureListener.CLOSE/CLOSE_ON_FAILURE are continuations of the write Task on Common's CLR-only EventExecutorTaskScheduler over ctx.Executor (owner decision 2026-11-24; the scheduler of handler's IdleStateHandler too, docs/handler-porting.md, Listener timing): the Transport completes its operation Tasks with RunContinuationsAsynchronously (src/Netty.NET.Transport/Channels/AbstractChannel.cs), so a continuation on TaskScheduler.Default ran later on a thread-pool thread and HttpServerKeepAliveHandlerTest saw the channel still open (43 of 49 cases failed, measured), while Java's DefaultPromise notifies the listener at once when the write completes on the event loop; the scheduler runs the continuation at once on the event loop (EmbeddedEventLoop.InEventLoop is always true, src/Netty.NET.Transport/Channels/Embedded/EmbeddedEventLoop.cs) and otherwise hands it to Execute. The static import of HttpUtil.* is using static HttpUtil; String.regionMatches(true, 0, MULTIPART_PREFIX, 0, n) is string.Compare(..., StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) == 0 over the prefix length (a shorter value does not match, as regionMatches returns false out of bounds).

The nested interfaces take the I prefix (ISourceCodec, IUpgradeCodec, IUpgradeCodecFactory); UpgradeEvent implements IReferenceCounted with narrowed Retain/Touch and explicit interface members; Collection<CharSequence> is ICollection<ICharSequence> and the request header strings are StringCharSequence; ChannelFutureListener.CLOSE_ON_FAILURE is a synchronous continuation that closes the channel when the write did not succeed (the mapping recorded in Transport AbstractBootstrap); Character.isWhitespace keeps the Java rule (HttpVersion.IsJavaWhitespace); StringBuilder.setLength is the Length setter.

The Java enum with constructor, fields, methods and the UNKNOWN constant-specific class body is a class with static readonly instances (as codec-base Base64Dialect and handler LogLevel); UNKNOWN is a private nested subclass overriding the virtual contains(int); ToString() returns the constant name; valueOf(int)/valueOf(CharSequence) are ValueOf(int)/ValueOf(ICharSequence); the package-private defaultReasonPhrase() is internal. review.scope: Static class. java.net.URI is System.Uri (toString() is OriginalString); Charset is Encoding, ISO_8859_1 is Encoding.Latin1, Charset.forName is Common's CharsetUtil.ForName (the Java charset names and aliases, so "charset=UTF8" gives UTF-8 as in Java, measured, where Encoding.GetEncoding threw and the default was returned), whose ArgumentException replaces IllegalCharsetNameException/UnsupportedCharsetException; Long.parseLong is the internal ParseLong (FormatException also for overflow); InetSocketAddress is EndPoint (unresolved DnsEndPoint, resolved IPEndPoint whose host string is the numeric address via NetUtil.GetHostname); normalizeAndGetContentLength takes the generic IList<T> for List<? extends CharSequence> (HttpObjectDecoder passes strings) and prints the list as AbstractCollection.toString(); String.trim() is the internal TrimJava; isValidTokenChar reads the octet as sbyte to keep the Java "octet < 0" test (Java byte sign rule). The @Deprecated members whose @deprecated text names their replacement are not ported (owner decision 2026-11-16); their comments are recorded below.

Comparable is IComparable<HttpVersion>; String.compareTo is string.CompareOrdinal; the text == HTTP_1_1_STRING fast paths are ReferenceEquals on the interned literals; toUpperCase(Locale.US) is ToUpperInvariant (invariant casing rules, so the Turkish dotted I never appears); Character.isISOControl is char.IsControl (same code points) and Character.isWhitespace keeps the Java rule in IsJavaWhitespace (char.IsWhiteSpace also accepts the no-break spaces Java excludes; internal because HttpServerUpgradeHandler reuses it); the package-private valueOf(String, boolean), constructor and encode(ByteBuf) are internal; encode writes text with ByteBufUtil.WriteAscii (AsciiString.c2b per char, as Java's writeCharSequence(US_ASCII)); numbers in text use the invariant culture.

Java interfaces take the I prefix; the re-declarations that only narrow return types (copy/duplicate/retainedDuplicate/replace/retain/touch, setProtocolVersion/setMethod/setUri/setStatus) are inherited from IByteBufHolder/IHttpMessage, because C# 9 covariant returns cover class overrides only (owner decision 2026-11-19, docs/transport-porting.md Decisions); the classes narrow them with covariant override returns and implement the interface members declared with other return types explicitly. EMPTY_LAST_CONTENT is a static readonly interface field and its anonymous class the private nested EmptyLastHttpContent, as codec-stomp ILastStompContentSubframe; its @Deprecated getDecoderResult() override is not ported (see HttpObject); DecoderResult.SUCCESS is reached through global:: because DecoderResult is the method inside the class; UnsupportedOperationException is NotSupportedException.

Public class with the Java constructors, path()/parameters()/rawPath()/rawQuery()/uri(), the static decodeComponent overloads and the nested Builder. Charset is System.Text.Encoding and new String(bytes, 0, n, charset) is Encoding.GetString (replacement fallback, as the JDK decoder). java.net.URI is System.Uri: URI.getRawPath()/getRawQuery() return the components exactly as written, while Uri.AbsolutePath normalizes them (an empty path of "http://localhost:8080?a=b" becomes "/"), so the private CLR helper RawPathAndQuery reads the path and query of Uri.OriginalString with the RFC 3986 generic syntax (scheme ":" ["//" authority] path ["?" query] ["#" fragment]); an opaque URI has neither, as java.net.URI reports null for both. Map<String, List<String>> is IDictionary<string, IList<string>>: LinkedHashMap is the Common LinkedHashMap (insertion order), Collections.emptyMap() is ImmutableDictionary.Empty, Collections.singletonList is a one-element ImmutableList, and "values instanceof ArrayList" is "values is List<string>". The labeled "break loop" is a goto to a label after the loop and the fall-through from ';' to '&' is goto case (docs/codec-compression-porting.md). PlatformDependent.allocateUninitializedArray is GC.AllocateUninitializedArray. The static builder() clashes with the nested Builder type (CS0102) and is Builder_() (owner rule); the private constructor and fields of the nested Builder that the decoder uses are internal. IllegalArgumentException is ArgumentException (StringUtil.decodeHexByte is the Common DecodeHexByte with the Java message), numbers in messages use the invariant culture.

Public class with the two constructors, addParam, toUri() and toString(). Charset is System.Text.Encoding; CharsetUtil.UTF_8.equals(charset) compares canonical charset names, so the CLR test is the code page (65001 for every UTF8Encoding) and any UTF-8 encoding takes the built-in UTF-8 path. String.getBytes(charset) is Encoding.GetBytes, which writes no preamble (the preamble "can be prefixed to the sequence of bytes resulting from the encoding process"), while the JDK "UTF-16" charset "writes a big-endian byte-order mark" when encoding; no .NET Encoding emits a byte-order mark from GetBytes. The private encode methods take the String arguments of addParam as string. toUri() is new Uri(ToString(), UriKind.RelativeOrAbsolute) (java.net.URI parses relative and absolute references) and URISyntaxException is the UriFormatException of the constructor. Character.isHighSurrogate/isLowSurrogate/toCodePoint are char.IsHighSurrogate/IsLowSurrogate/ConvertToUtf32. The encoded octets are masked with & 0xF in forDigit, so the signed Java byte and the C# byte give the same hex digits.

CharSequence is ICharSequence and String is string; both Java overloads are kept, and the String values compared or stored as CharSequence are wrapped in the Common StringCharSequence because a C# string is not an ICharSequence; Integer/Short/Long results are int?/short?/long?; Iterable<?> is IEnumerable<object> (a value-type IEnumerable binds to the Object overload); Map.Entry and Iterator are the codec-base IEntry and IIterator (docs/codec-base-porting.md, Headers). @UnstableApi has no counterpart; CharSequence... is params ICharSequence[]; AbstractMap.SimpleImmutableEntry is the private nested ImmutableEntry with Map.Entry equality; LinkedHashSet is the Common LinkedHashSet; the inner iterator classes receive the name/value array; NoSuchElementException is InvalidOperationException (codec-base IIterator contract); iterator() is IteratorAsString().

Public sealed class with STRICT/LAX and decode(String) as Decode returning ICookie; the private nested CookieBuilder keeps its members (package-private ones are internal). The labeled "break loop" is a goto to a label after the loop (as the core QueryStringDecoder). String.regionMatches(true, offset, name, 0, len) is string.Compare with StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase over len: the number of characters compared is the lesser of the substring lengths and len, and a shorter region compares unequal (measured), so a region at the end of the header does not match, as in Java. java.util.Date is DateTimeOffset (codec-base DateFormatter, which parses the header through a StringCharSequence); Date.getTime() and System.currentTimeMillis() are ToUnixTimeMilliseconds() and DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.ToUnixTimeMilliseconds() (as handler PcapWriter). Long.parseLong is the core HttpUtil.ParseLong (NumberFormatException is FormatException); Java throws NumberFormatException for a null string too, while long.Parse throws ArgumentNullException, so setMaxAge ignores both (a valueless Max-Age attribute stays a session cookie as in Java).

Public sealed class with STRICT/LAX and the encode overloads: encode(String, String), encode(Cookie), encode(Cookie...) as params ICookie[], encode(Collection<? extends Cookie>) as the covariant IReadOnlyCollection<ICookie> and encode(Iterable<? extends Cookie>) as IEnumerable<ICookie>, so a List<DefaultCookie> binds as the Java wildcard allows (a collection without IReadOnlyCollection<T>, such as ISet<T>, takes the Iterable overload, which encodes the same text). The package-private COOKIE_COMPARATOR is an internal IComparer<ICookie>, and its anonymous Comparator is the private nested CookieComparator. Arrays.sort(T[], Comparator) is stable while Array.Sort is unstable, so the sorted copies use Enumerable.OrderBy (a stable sort), which keeps the creation order of cookies with paths of the same length as the Java comment requires. InternalThreadLocalMap.get().arrayList() is an operation-owned List. Iterator.hasNext()/next() is IEnumerator.MoveNext()/Current (do/while loops after the first element; the enumerator is disposed).

Public interface ICookie (Java interfaces take the I prefix) with the Java methods name()/value()/setValue/wrap()/setWrap/domain()/setDomain/path()/setPath/maxAge()/setMaxAge/isSecure()/setSecure/isHttpOnly()/setHttpOnly as methods. Comparable<Cookie> is IComparable<ICookie> (CompareTo keeps its BCL name). The interface constant UNDEFINED_MAX_AGE is a C# interface constant (long.MinValue); implementing classes name it ICookie.UNDEFINED_MAX_AGE, because static interface members are not inherited into a class.

Abstract class with the protected initCookie(...) as InitCookie returning DefaultCookie. CharBuffer.wrap(header, valueBegin, valueEnd), a read-only CharSequence view of the region, is the Common StringCharSequence(header, offset, count) view. The logger field initializer calls getClass(); a C# field initializer cannot reference instance members (CS0236), so the constructor initializes it with GetType() before the strict flag. String.substring(begin, end) is Substring(begin, end - begin); the logger calls keep their {} formats.

Abstract class with the protected strict field and the protected validateCookie(String, String) as ValidateCookie. The String name and value reach the CharSequence helpers of CookieUtil as StringCharSequence views (a C# string is not an ICharSequence). IllegalArgumentException is ArgumentException; the invalid char is appended as a char, as the Java string concatenation does.

The final class with a private constructor is a static class (as the core HttpConstants) and its String constants are const strings. The nested enum SameSite has the static method of(String), which a C# enum cannot declare, so it is a sealed class with the static readonly instances Lax, Strict and None and a private constructor, as codec-base Base64Dialect (docs/codec-base-porting.md); name() is Name(), ToString() returns the constant name, getEnumConstants() is a private VALUES array in declaration order, and the package-private of(String) is internal. equalsIgnoreCase is string.Equals with StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase.

Package-private final class with a private constructor: an internal static class with internal members. java.util.BitSet is BitArray sized to the ASCII range (128 bits). BitSet.get(int) is false past the set's size, while BitArray.Get(int) throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException for an index not less than its length, so firstInvalidOctet checks the length first (as codec-base DateFormatter.IsDelim). CharSequence is the Common ICharSequence and the "" of unwrapValue is StringCharSequence.Empty. InternalThreadLocalMap.get().stringBuilder() was retired from the Common port as a JVM allocation cache, and its cookie users take an operation-owned StringBuilder (docs/common-clr-design.md, Operation-owned CSV storage); the callers name it CookieUtil.StringBuilder(), because a using static import would make it ambiguous with System.Text.StringBuilder. String.trim() is the core HttpUtil.TrimJava (chars up to U+0020); IllegalArgumentException is ArgumentException; StringBuilder.append(long) is the invariant-culture text of the number.

Public class with the Java methods; the members of the non-final class are virtual. ObjectUtil.checkNotNull/checkNonEmptyAfterTrim are the Common CheckNotNull/CheckNonEmptyAfterTrim (ArgumentNullException/ArgumentException). equals/hashCode/compareTo are Equals/GetHashCode/CompareTo; String.compareTo is string.CompareOrdinal and String.equals the ordinal string.Equals. equalsIgnoreCase and compareToIgnoreCase fold each char with Character.toLowerCase(Character.toUpperCase(c)); the private CompareToIgnoreCase keeps that fold with char.ToUpperInvariant/ToLowerInvariant, because StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase only uppercases and orders '_' (and the other chars between 'Z' and 'a') after the letters (measured: Compare("_", "a", OrdinalIgnoreCase) is positive, Java's compareToIgnoreCase is negative); one measured difference remains: ToUpperInvariant leaves U+0131 (dotless i) unchanged, where Character.toUpperCase maps it to 'I' (cookie domains are ASCII). The @Deprecated validateValue(String, String), whose @deprecated text ("CookieUtil is package private, will be removed once old Cookie API is dropped") names no replacement, is ported as protected virtual with [Obsolete] and that text. @Deprecated members whose @deprecated text names no replacement are ported with [Obsolete("<the @deprecated text>")], and @Deprecated without @deprecated text with [Obsolete] (owner decision 2026-11-16). toString() appends the long maxAge as invariant-culture text and SameSite through its ToString().

Public sealed class with STRICT/LAX, decodeAll(String) as DecodeAll returning IList<ICookie> and decode(String) as Decode returning ISet<ICookie>; the private decode(Collection<? super Cookie>, String) takes ICollection<ICookie>. TreeSet with the natural ordering is SortedSet with the default comparer (IComparable<ICookie>): TreeSet compares with compareTo and add leaves the set unchanged for an equal element, SortedSet.Add returns false for an element already present, so the first cookie of a name wins in both. Collections.unmodifiableList is a ReadOnlyCollection<T> view (as codec-socks SocksInitRequest). The labeled "break loop" is a goto; regionMatches is string.Compare with OrdinalIgnoreCase/Ordinal over the length (see ClientCookieDecoder).

Public sealed class with STRICT/LAX and the encode overloads mapped as in ClientCookieEncoder (List<String> is IList<string>, Collections.emptyList() is ImmutableList<string>.Empty). Map<String, Integer> is Dictionary<string, int>, and "map.put(name, i) != null" is the private CLR helper Put, which reports whether a previous mapping existed and replaces it. java.util.Date is DateTimeOffset (codec-base DateFormatter); new Date(maxAge * 1000 + now) is DateTimeOffset.FromUnixTimeMilliseconds, whose range ends at -62,135,596,800,000 and 253,402,300,799,999 ms (years 1 to 9999). A java.util.Date has no such bound, so an Expires instant beyond it (a Max-Age above about 7,975 years) is clamped to the range by the private NewDate, where Java prints a year above 9999; the Max-Age attribute is unchanged. maxAge * 1000 wraps as Java's long arithmetic does (unchecked).

review.scope: Public sealed class with the Java query methods (isCorsSupportEnabled() ... isShortCircuit()) and the internal constructor that copies a CorsConfigBuilder. Set<T> is ISet<T>; LinkedHashSet is the Common LinkedHashSet (insertion order: origin() returns the first configured origin); Collections.unmodifiableSet is a ReadOnlySet<T> view (as handler SslUtils). Callable<?> is Func<object> (see CorsConfigBuilder) and "value instanceof Iterable" is "value is IEnumerable<object>", the core mapping of Iterable<?> (a string or ICharSequence is not one, as a Java String is not Iterable; a sequence of a value type is added as one object). IllegalStateException is InvalidOperationException. toString() keeps the Java text through the private CLR helpers JavaString (true/false), CollectionToString (AbstractCollection.toString, "[a, b]") and MapToString (AbstractMap.toString, "{k=v}"); a Func value prints its delegate type name where Java prints the Callable's class name and identity hash. In preflightResponseHeaders() the emptiness test names the field this.preflightHeaders, because C# forbids a simple name that a later local of the same block hides (CS0844). The @Deprecated isShortCurcuit(), withAnyOrigin(), withOrigin(String), withOrigins(String...) and the nested Builder name their replacements (isShortCircuit(), CorsConfigBuilder) and are not ported; their comments are recorded below. The @Deprecated DateValueGenerator ("Removed without alternatives.") is ported as a public sealed nested class with [Obsolete] and its Call() returning DateTimeOffset. @Deprecated members whose @deprecated text names no replacement are ported with [Obsolete("<the @deprecated text>")], and @Deprecated without @deprecated text with [Obsolete] (owner decision 2026-11-16).

Public sealed class with forAnyOrigin()/forOrigin(String)/forOrigins(String...) and the chained configuration methods; the package-private fields and constructors are internal. java.util.concurrent.Callable<T> is Func<T>, the Common mapping of the executor submissions (EventExecutorExtensions.SubmitAsync(Func<T>)), and Map<CharSequence, Callable<?>> is Dictionary<ICharSequence, Func<object>>. Func<TResult> is covariant only for reference types, so preflightResponseHeader(CharSequence, Callable<T>) stores a Func<T> of a reference type as it is and wraps one of a value type (the date generator's Func<DateTimeOffset>) in a boxing lambda. ConstantValueGenerator and DateValueGenerator keep call() as Call(), the map holds their method-group delegates, and the private constructor of the private ConstantValueGenerator is internal (a C# outer class cannot reach a nested private member). preflightResponseHeader(CharSequence, Iterable<T>) takes IEnumerable<object> (the core mapping of Iterable<?>), because a generic IEnumerable<T> would also bind a string argument (IEnumerable<char>); Arrays.asList(values) is the object[] passed as IEnumerable<object> (the cast selects that overload instead of the params overload itself). String.../CharSequence.../HttpMethod... are params arrays (a call without arguments is ambiguous between the String and CharSequence overloads in C#, where Java picks String...). Collections.emptySet() is ImmutableHashSet<string>.Empty; a HashMap accepts a null key where a Dictionary throws ArgumentNullException, so a null header name fails when configured. checkNotNullWithIAE is the Common CheckNotNullWithIAE (ArgumentException). new Date() is the current instant at millisecond precision.

Public class CorsHandler : ChannelDuplexHandler with the two constructors (List<CorsConfig> is IList<CorsConfig>, Collections.singletonList a one-element ImmutableList). write(ctx, msg, promise) is WriteAsync, whose Task replaces the promise (docs/codec-base-porting.md). ChannelFutureListener.CLOSE on the writeAndFlush future of respond(...) is a continuation that closes the channel on Common's EventExecutorTaskScheduler over ctx.Executor (CLR-only, owner decision 2026-11-24), the scheduler of the core HttpServerKeepAliveHandler/HttpServerExpectContinueHandler and of handler's IdleStateHandler (docs/handler-porting.md, Listener timing): the close runs at once when the write completes on the event loop, which shortCircuitWithConnectionCloseShouldClose and preflightRequestWithConnectionCloseShouldClose check right after writeInbound. getForOrigin tests a null origin before Set.contains: Java's LinkedHashSet.contains(null) is false, the Common LinkedHashSet looks it up in a Dictionary whose ContainsKey throws ArgumentNullException for null. String header values bind to the HttpHeaders Set/Add(ICharSequence, object) overloads, and the Set<T> results of CorsConfig to the Iterable overloads (IEnumerable<object>).

review.scope: Public abstract class. java.io.File is FileInfo and RandomAccessFile with its FileChannel one FileStream (docs/handler-porting.md, java.io and NIO); the java.io.File results that the code tests are AbstractDiskHttpData's CLR helpers FileLength (length(), 0 for a missing file, where FileInfo.Length throws and caches until Refresh()), FileExists, CreateNewFile (FileMode.CreateNew, false for an existing file), DeleteFile and RenameFile (File.Move, false on failure), and OpenFile, which opens the RandomAccessFile modes "r"/"rw" as FileMode.Open/OpenOrCreate with the JDK's Windows sharing FILE_SHARE_READ | FILE_SHARE_WRITE (FileShare.ReadWrite) and without a FileStream buffer, so a second channel reads what an open channel wrote. force(false) is Flush(true). File.getPath() is FullName (the temporary files have absolute paths). PlatformDependent.createTempFile is the Common PlatformDependent.CreateTempFile(string, string, DirectoryInfo) (docs/common-clr-design.md, Native temporary-file creation). getBytes(index, FileChannel, position, length) is ByteBuf.GetBytes(int, Stream, int), which writes the whole range at the stream position (the Java loop only repeats partial channel writes); the SafeFileHandle overload is not used because reading FileStream.SafeFileHandle "automatically flushes the stream and sets the current stream position to 0". FileChannel.read(ByteBuffer) of -1 is Stream.Read of 0, the NIO ByteBuffers are byte arrays, wrappedBuffer(flipped buffer) is WrappedBuffer(array, 0, read), and transferTo(position, count, target) is the private TransferTo helper (positional read, write at the target position, input position restored). Integer.toString(diskFilename.hashCode()) keeps Java's String.hashCode value (JavaHashCode), because string.GetHashCode() is not stable across runs. getBaseDirectory()/deleteOnExit() are protected internal, as DefaultHttpDataFactoryTest calls them from the package (Java protected admits the package; docs/codec-base-porting.md, Package access); the logger is the Common InternalLoggerFactory logger.

Public abstract class over the Common AbstractReferenceCounted (refCnt() is RefCnt, deallocate() Deallocate()). Charset is Encoding (HttpConstants.DEFAULT_CHARSET is Encoding.UTF8); cleanName keeps Character.isWhitespace as core's HttpVersion.IsJavaWhitespace; checkNonEmpty is ObjectUtil.CheckNonEmpty (ArgumentException); content() is the virtual Content property, which wraps the IOException in the Transport ChannelException. retain()/retain(int) and the abstract touch()/touch(Object) narrow the AbstractReferenceCounted members with covariant override returns. A Java abstract class need not declare the interface methods it leaves to its subclasses; C# must map every IHttpData member, so getHttpDataType(), compareTo(InterfaceHttpData), the content mutators/accessors and copy()/duplicate()/retainedDuplicate()/replace(ByteBuf) are declared abstract, and the IByteBufHolder members (declared with their own return types) are implemented explicitly, as core's DefaultHttpContent does.

The package-private final class is internal sealed and keeps both license headers (Netty and the Hoehrmann DFA). It implements ByteProcessor, which is Func<byte, bool> in the Common port (src/Netty.NET.Common/ByteProcessor.cs), through Process(byte): buffer.forEachByte(this) is ForEachByte(Process), as core's HttpChunkLineValidatingByteProcessor does; the package-private check(ByteBuf, int, int) is internal and the int constants are const. Java byte sign (owner decision: ByteBuf GetByte/ReadByte return the unsigned System.Byte): TYPES[b & 0xFF] is TYPES[b]; b & 0x3f and (0xff >> type) & b give the same values for the signed Java byte and the unsigned octet, because both masks clear the bits that sign extension sets. Public class over codec-base's ReplayingDecoder implementing IWebSocketFrameDecoder. ReplayingDecoder<Void> is ReplayingDecoder<object> (C# needs a type argument; test/Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Tests/ReplayingDecoderTest.cs records the same mapping), decode overrides Decode, and the package-private DEFAULT_MAX_FRAME_SIZE is an internal const. Java byte sign (owner decision: ByteBuf GetByte/ReadByte return the unsigned System.Byte): type == (byte) 0xFF is type == 0xFF, and the masks (type & 0x80, b & 0x7f, b & 0x80) give the same values as for the signed Java byte; the seven length bits are widened as uint before the OR into the long frame size (CS0675; the value is never negative). The static import ByteBufUtil.readBytes is using static ByteBufUtil: the Buffer port's ByteBufUtil.ReadBytes(alloc, buffer, length) reads through buffer.ReadBytes(dst), which the replaying buffer supports, when the allocator returns exactly length writable bytes (every Netty.NET allocator), as Java does (src/Netty.NET.Buffer/ByteBufUtil.cs, src/Netty.NET.Handler.Codec/ReplayingDecoderByteBuf.cs). The private ReadBytes copy of the Java body that stood for it was removed on 2026-11-24 (ByteBufUtil.ReadBytes called ReadBytes(dst, length), which ReplayingDecoderByteBuf rejects as Java's does, and the two WebSocketClientHandshaker00Test cases that decode a 00 frame failed with "not a replayable operation"). IllegalArgumentException is ArgumentException, and numbers in messages use the invariant culture.

The package-private nested enum State is an internal nested C# enum. C# switch sections cannot fall through ("control can't fall through from one switch section to the next ... To imitate the fall-through behavior ... you can use the goto statement", https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/statements/selection-statements), so each state that continues into the next ends with goto case; the unreachable default's throw new Error(...) is UnreachableException, as AssertionError is in the handler port (docs/handler-porting.md, Exceptions). Java byte sign (owner decision: ByteBuf GetByte/ReadByte return the unsigned System.Byte): the masks of the first and second octet ((b & 0x80) != 0, (b & 0x70) >> 4, b & 0x0F, b & 0x7F) give the same values as for the signed Java byte, and unmask XORs the unsigned octet, whose low eight bits SetByte writes as Java's setByte does; getShort returns the signed short in the Buffer port as in Java, so checkCloseFrameBody sees the same, possibly negative, status code (isValidStatusCode accepts code < 0, as in Java). The Buffer port has no ByteBuf.order(): buffers are big-endian and byte order is chosen by explicit BE/LE accessors (docs/codec-base-porting.md, Byte order; src/Netty.NET.Handler.Codec/ReplayingDecoderByteBuf.cs records order() as not ported), so the ByteOrder lookups and the LITTLE_ENDIAN mask reversal, which Java needs only for deprecated swapped buffers, have no counterpart (a CLR comment marks the place). ByteBufUtil.readBytes(alloc, in, n) is the Buffer port's ByteBufUtil.ReadBytes (the cumulation is an ordinary buffer here). ctx.writeAndFlush(...).addListener(ChannelFutureListener.CLOSE) closes ctx.Channel (a Task carries no channel) from a synchronous continuation of the write Task on TaskScheduler.Default, as codec-base MessageAggregator does (docs/codec-base-porting.md, MessageAggregator: "Future listeners are Task continuations that run synchronously"); with ExecuteSynchronously, "If the antecedent is already complete when the continuation is created, the continuation will run on the thread that creates the continuation" (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.threading.tasks.taskcontinuationoptions?view=net-10.0), as a listener added to a completed future runs at once, so the EmbeddedChannel tests see the channel closed right after the call. UnsupportedOperationException is NotSupportedException, the byte opcodes are const, the trace logger is the Common IInternalLogger, numbers in messages use the invariant culture, and checkCloseFrameBody is protected virtual because the Java method is overridable.

Public abstract class with the Java constructors and members. java.net.URI is System.Uri, as in core (QueryStringDecoder, HttpUtil). java.net.URI keeps every component as written: getHost() returns the host "or null if the host is undefined" (with the brackets of an IPv6 literal and its case), getPort() "or -1 if the port is undefined", getRawPath()/getRawQuery() the raw components or null, and toString() the original input string (https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/net/URI.html). System.Uri canonicalizes: Host throws InvalidOperationException for a relative URI (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.uri.host?view=net-10.0), ToString() returns the canonical form with a lower-cased host, and OriginalString is "the exact URI specified when this instance was constructed" (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.uri.originalstring?view=net-10.0). The private UriComponents helper of WebSocketClientHandshaker therefore reads scheme, host, port, raw path and raw query from Uri.OriginalString with the generic syntax [scheme:][//authority][path][?query][#fragment] (a scheme not followed by '/' is opaque; a server-based authority is [userinfo@]host[:port]; an empty port is undefined, a non-numeric port makes host and port undefined), as core's QueryStringDecoder reads the raw path and query, and toString() is OriginalString. The helper does not reject a host that java.net.URI would treat as registry-based (for example one with '_'), where getHost() is null in Java. URI.create(s)/new URI(s) is new Uri(s, UriKind.RelativeOrAbsolute), which accepts the relative references ("/ws", "//localhost/") the tests use. ChannelFuture is Task and ChannelPromise is TaskCompletionSource (docs/transport-porting.md: promise arguments are the returned Task; docs/handler-porting.md, Task promises): the promise overloads take the TaskCompletionSource that the method completes and return its Task, channel.newPromise()/ctx.newPromise() is a new TaskCompletionSource without RunContinuationsAsynchronously (so a listener added with ExecuteSynchronously runs when the promise completes, as DefaultPromise notifies at once on the event loop), setSuccess/setFailure are SetResult/SetException, trySuccess/tryFailure TrySetResult/TrySetException, isDone() Task.IsCompleted, and future.cause() is copied with TrySetFromTask, which "attempts to transition the underlying Task<TResult> into the same completion state as the specified completedTask" (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.threading.tasks.taskcompletionsource.trysetfromtask?view=net-10.0). Listeners are synchronous continuations on TaskScheduler.Default (docs/codec-base-porting.md, MessageAggregator); ChannelFutureListener.CLOSE closes future.channel(), which a Task does not carry, so the continuation closes the channel the operation ran on. The Task-returning methods take the Async suffix (handshake is HandshakeAsync, close is CloseAsync, processHandshake is ProcessHandshakeAsync, sendUnsupportedVersionResponse is SendUnsupportedVersionResponseAsync). String.split(",") keeps Java's result in a private Split helper ("Trailing empty strings are therefore not included in the resulting array"; "If the expression does not match any part of the input then the resulting array has just one element, namely this string", https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/lang/String.html), and trim() (code points up to U+0020) is core's HttpUtil.TrimJava. String.format("Invalid subprotocol. Actual: %s. Expected one of: %s", ...) is a concatenation with "null" for null, and toLowerCase(Locale.US) of the origin host is ToLowerInvariant (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.string.tolowerinvariant?view=net-10.0). AsciiString.contentEquals(scheme) of the HttpScheme/WebSocketScheme names is a private ContentEquals that is false for null as in Java; NetUtil.toSocketAddressString(host, port) is the Common NetUtil.ToSocketAddressString, which keeps the brackets of an IPv6 host. The package-private static websocketHostValue/websocketOriginValue return CharSequence in Java but always a String, so they are internal and return string. C# does not allow a volatile long, so forceCloseTimeoutMillis is read and written with Volatile.Read/Write, and the AtomicIntegerFieldUpdater compareAndSet(this, 0, 1) is Interlocked.CompareExchange(ref forceCloseInit, 1, 0). ctx.executor().schedule(...)/channel.eventLoop().schedule(...) is ScheduleAsync (src/Netty.NET.Common/Concurrent/EventExecutorSchedulingExtensions.cs), and the Future<?> is the CancellationTokenSource whose token was passed, cancel(false) being Cancel() (docs/handler-porting.md, Executors and scheduling). The anonymous handshake response handler is the named private nested class HandshakeResponseHandler and the anonymous Runnables are lambdas; channel.eventLoop().execute is EventLoop.Execute. The protected members that the Java tests call through package access have internal forwarders (Invoke...), as core's HttpObjectEncoder.InvokeEncodeInitialLine and codec-base's MessageToMessageDecoder.InvokeDecode (docs/codec-base-porting.md, Package access). Non-final Java methods are virtual; pipeline.get/context/remove(Class) are Get<T>(), Context(Type) and Remove<T>(); HttpClientCodec.removeOutboundHandler() is the Transport CombinedChannelDuplexHandler member. IllegalStateException is InvalidOperationException, IllegalArgumentException ArgumentException, ClosedChannelException the Transport type and assert Debug.Assert.

The package-private abstract class is public because the public WebSocketServerProtocolHandler and WebSocketClientProtocolHandler derive from it and a C# base class must be at least as accessible as the derived class (CS0060, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/misc/cs0060); its constructors stay internal. MessageToMessageDecoder<WebSocketFrame> is the codec-base generic and super(WebSocketFrame.class) is base(typeof(WebSocketFrame)); ChannelOutboundHandler is the Transport IChannelOutboundHandler whose operations return the Task that replaces the promise (docs/codec-base-porting.md, Outbound operations). The ChannelPromise closeSent is a TaskCompletionSource completed by this handler: write(CloseWebSocketFrame) returns its Task where Java uses the caller's promise.unvoid() (no void promise), a write after the close frame returns a faulted Task (ClosedChannelException), PromiseNotifier(false, ...) is a continuation that copies the outcome with TrySetFromTask (docs/common-task-composition.md, PromiseNotifier), and close(ctx, promise) returns the Task of ctx.close() started once closeSent completes. The listeners on the close-frame write and on closeSent run on Common's CLR-only EventExecutorTaskScheduler over ctx.Executor (owner decision 2026-11-24), the DefaultPromise.notifyListeners() timing that handler's IdleStateHandler and core's HttpServerKeepAliveHandler use too (docs/handler-porting.md, Listener timing): the Transport completes the write Task with RunContinuationsAsynchronously when the later flush writes it, so with TaskScheduler.Default the close ran later on a thread-pool thread and WebSocketServerProtocolHandlerTest saw the channel still open after close() (measured: 5 of 6 runs had one or two such failures; with the scheduler 0 of 8). ctx.executor().schedule(...)/channel.eventLoop().schedule(...) is ScheduleAsync (src/Netty.NET.Common/Concurrent/EventExecutorSchedulingExtensions.cs), and the Future<?> is the CancellationTokenSource whose token was passed, cancel(false) being Cancel() (docs/handler-porting.md, Executors and scheduling). ctx.channel().config().isAutoRead() is Config.IsAutoRead(), SocketAddress is EndPoint, and the package-private closeSent/applyCloseSentTimeout are internal (the subclasses call them).

ChannelFuture is Task and ChannelPromise is TaskCompletionSource (docs/transport-porting.md: promise arguments are the returned Task; docs/handler-porting.md, Task promises): the promise overloads take the TaskCompletionSource that the method completes and return its Task, channel.newPromise()/ctx.newPromise() is a new TaskCompletionSource without RunContinuationsAsynchronously (so a listener added with ExecuteSynchronously runs when the promise completes, as DefaultPromise notifies at once on the event loop), setSuccess/setFailure are SetResult/SetException, trySuccess/tryFailure TrySetResult/TrySetException, isDone() Task.IsCompleted, and future.cause() is copied with TrySetFromTask, which "attempts to transition the underlying Task<TResult> into the same completion state as the specified completedTask" (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.threading.tasks.taskcompletionsource.trysetfromtask?view=net-10.0). String.split(",") keeps Java's result in a private Split helper ("Trailing empty strings are therefore not included in the resulting array"; "If the expression does not match any part of the input then the resulting array has just one element, namely this string", https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/lang/String.html), and trim() (code points up to U+0020) is core's HttpUtil.TrimJava. The protected members that the Java tests call through package access have internal forwarders (Invoke...), as core's HttpObjectEncoder.InvokeEncodeInitialLine and codec-base's MessageToMessageDecoder.InvokeDecode (docs/codec-base-porting.md, Package access). Non-final Java methods are virtual; SUB_PROTOCOL_WILDCARD is a const; IllegalStateException is InvalidOperationException, ClosedChannelException the Transport type and assert Debug.Assert.

The static imports of HttpMethod.GET and HttpVersion.HTTP_1_1 are using static. java.util.regex.Pattern is System.Text.RegularExpressions.Regex with the same patterns, and matcher(s).replaceAll("") is Regex.Replace(s, ""), which replaces all matches (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.text.regularexpressions.regex.replace?view=net-10.0). Long.parseLong is core's HttpUtil.ParseLong (FormatException); the long division by a zero space count throws DivideByZeroException where Java throws ArithmeticException, and the (int) casts keep the low 32 bits (unchecked). The Buffer port has no array() (docs/buffer-porting.md, Array extraction), so the 16-byte array that Java wraps and reads back with input.array() is kept in a local and handed to WebSocketUtil.Md5. The CharSequence returned by HttpHeaders.get(...) is a string: AsciiString.contentEqualsIgnoreCase(String) wraps it in the Common StringCharSequence (core notes, CharSequence and String), CharSequence.equals(String) is string.Equals, and a null header is printed as "null", as Java string concatenation and String.format("%s") do (C# concatenation prints nothing for null). Set.toString() of headers().names() is built with string.Join as "[a, b]". The [Obsolete] uri() of WebSocketServerHandshaker is still the Location value, so its two calls disable CS0612 with that reason. The close overrides write the frame and complete the caller's promise with TrySetFromTask, as writeAndFlush(frame, promise) does.

ServerHandshakeStateEvent is a simple C# enum; its @Deprecated constant HANDSHAKE_COMPLETE, whose @deprecated text names the HandshakeComplete class, is not ported (owner decision 2026-11-16), so the handshake handler fires only the HandshakeComplete event (owner review: users listening for the enum constant get the class event instead). ChannelFutureListener.CLOSE is a synchronous continuation that closes ctx.Channel. cause.getMessage().getBytes() encodes with the platform default charset, which "typically depends upon the locale and charset of the underlying operating system" (https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/nio/charset/Charset.html); the port uses Encoding.UTF8. buildHandshakeException narrows the return type with a C# 9 covariant override.

The package-private class is internal. The ChannelPromise handshakePromise is a TaskCompletionSource (see WebSocketClientHandshaker); the handshake listener is a synchronous continuation on TaskScheduler.Default and future.cause() is the Task's InnerException. The deprecated ServerHandshakeStateEvent.HANDSHAKE_COMPLETE is not ported (see WebSocketServerProtocolHandler), so only the HandshakeComplete event follows the "Kept for compatibility" comment. ctx.executor().schedule(...)/channel.eventLoop().schedule(...) is ScheduleAsync (src/Netty.NET.Common/Concurrent/EventExecutorSchedulingExtensions.cs), and the Future<?> is the CancellationTokenSource whose token was passed, cancel(false) being Cancel() (docs/handler-porting.md, Executors and scheduling). ctx.flush().fireUserEventTriggered(...).close() are three calls, because the Transport's Flush() and FireUserEventTriggered() return the outbound/inbound invoker interfaces. The package-private final class is an internal sealed class with the private constructor (and its "// Unused" comment); its static methods are internal (md5 is Md5, sha1() and sha1(byte[]) are Sha1, base64 is Base64, randomBytes is RandomBytes, randomNumber is RandomNumber, byteAtIndex is ByteAtIndex). java.security.MessageDigest is System.Security.Cryptography.IncrementalHash, which "Provides support for computing a hash or HMAC value incrementally across several segments" (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.security.cryptography.incrementalhash?view=net-10.0): getInstance("MD5"/"SHA1") is IncrementalHash.CreateHash(HashAlgorithmName.MD5/SHA1); update(byte[]) is AppendData; digest() ("The digest is reset after this call is made", https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/security/MessageDigest.html) and digest(byte[]) (update, then digest()) are AppendData plus GetHashAndReset, which returns "to the state the object was in at construction". IncrementalHash has no reset() member, so GetHashAndReset() with the result dropped stands for reset(); WebSocketServerHandshaker13 uses the IncrementalHash returned by Sha1() as Java uses the MessageDigest. CreateHash throws CryptographicException when "hashAlgorithm is not a known hash algorithm" (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.security.cryptography.incrementalhash.createhash?view=net-10.0), which stands for NoSuchAlgorithmException; Java's InternalError (a JVM error) is InvalidOperationException with the Java message. The anonymous FastThreadLocal<MessageDigest> subclasses are the named private nested classes Md5Digest/Sha1Digest over the Common FastThreadLocal<IncrementalHash> (initialValue() is InitialValue()). Base64.getEncoder() is the Basic encoder (RFC 4648 Table 1 alphabet; it "does not add any line feed (line separator) character", https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/util/Base64.html); encodeToString is Convert.ToBase64String, whose digits are A-Z, a-z, 0-9, + and / with "=" for trailing padding and which inserts line breaks only through the Base64FormattingOptions overloads (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.convert.tobase64string?view=net-10.0). ThreadLocalRandom.current() is Random.Shared (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.random.shared?view=net-10.0): nextBytes is NextBytes and nextDouble() is NextDouble(), which "Returns a random floating-point number that is greater than or equal to 0.0, and less than 1.0" (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.random.nextdouble?view=net-10.0). assert is Debug.Assert; the int arithmetic of byteAtIndex is unchanged.

String.split(regex) with the literal "," or ";" keeps Java's result in the private Split helper: "Trailing empty strings are therefore not included in the resulting array" and "If the expression does not match any part of the input then the resulting array has just one element, namely this string" (https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/lang/String.html), where string.Split keeps trailing empty entries (so "a," gives one extension and "," none, as in Java). trim() removes the chars up to U+0020 and is core's internal HttpUtil.TrimJava. java.util.regex.Pattern is Regex with the same pattern; matcher.matches() is a whole-input match (the pattern is anchored by ^ and $ and the input is trimmed), and group(n), which returns null when the group "failed to match any part of the input sequence" (https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/util/regex/Matcher.html), is the group's Value only when Group.Success is true (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.text.regularexpressions.group.success?view=net-10.0; private helper GroupOrNull). Public class over the Transport ChannelDuplexHandler. write(ctx, msg, promise) is WriteAsync(ctx, msg, cancellationToken), whose Task replaces the promise (docs/codec-base-porting.md, Outbound operations); the protected onHttpResponseWrite(ctx, response, promise) keeps its name, takes the caller's CancellationToken and returns that Task, as handler's AbstractTrafficShapingHandler.SubmitWrite does; onHttpRequestChannelRead and isExtensionNegotiationEnabled are protected virtual. handlePotentialUpgrade adds two listeners to the caller's promise before the response is written: a TaskCompletionSource stands for that promise, the listeners are continuations of its Task, and the Task of base.WriteAsync completes it with TrySetFromTask, which copies "the completion status (including exception or cancellation information)" (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.threading.tasks.taskcompletionsource.trysetfromtask?view=net-10.0; docs/common-task-composition.md). Java's DefaultPromise notifies the listeners at once when the write completes on the event loop; the continuations therefore run on Common's CLR-only EventExecutorTaskScheduler over ctx.Executor (owner decision 2026-11-24; docs/handler-porting.md, Listener timing; handler's IdleStateHandler and core's HttpServerKeepAliveHandler use it too), so the pipeline is changed before writeOutbound returns. Measured: with TaskScheduler.Default, 10 to 11 of the 83 extension test cases failed in three runs. future.isSuccess() is IsCompletedSuccessfully. The varargs constructors take params arrays; Arrays.asList(checkNonEmpty(...)) is the array as an IList and checkPositive/checkNonEmpty are the Common ObjectUtil checks (ArgumentException). ArrayDeque is Queue (poll() of an empty queue is null through TryDequeue, offer is Enqueue), Collections.emptyList() an empty array, and IllegalStateException is InvalidOperationException with the number in the invariant culture. msg != LastHttpContent.EMPTY_LAST_CONTENT and msg != Unpooled.EMPTY_BUFFER are ReferenceEquals tests (ILastHttpContent.EMPTY_LAST_CONTENT, Unpooled.EmptyBuffer); ctx.close() is CloseAsync() with its Task discarded, as Java discards the ChannelFuture.

The package-private abstract class, its constructor, FRAME_TAIL and EMPTY_DEFLATE_BLOCK are internal. Java byte sign rule: the (byte) 0xff octets of FRAME_TAIL are the unsigned 0xFF of a C# byte, the same bits; the buffers are only written and compared byte for byte, never read as numbers. ZlibCodecFactory.newZlibDecoder(ZlibWrapper.NONE, maxAllocation) is codec-compression's JdkZlibDecoder over the internal Inflater stand-in on the BCL raw DeflateStream, fed in whole buffers for the NONE wrapper (docs/codec-compression-porting.md). EmbeddedChannel.builder().handlers(...).build() is new EmbeddedChannel.Builder().Handlers(...).Build(), readInbound()/readOutbound() are ReadInbound<ByteBuf>()/ReadOutbound<ByteBuf>(), ctx.alloc().compositeBuffer() is ctx.Alloc().CompositeBuffer(), addComponent(true, buf) is AddComponent(buf, true) (the Buffer port's parameter order), numComponents() is the NumComponents property and msg.getClass().getName() is GetType().FullName. EMPTY_DEFLATE_BLOCK.equals(content) is ByteBuf.Equals (readable bytes). handlerRemoved/channelInactive override the Transport ChannelHandlerAdapter/ChannelInboundHandlerAdapter members; decode is Decode with IList<object> @out. CodecException is codec-base's.

The package-private abstract class, its constructors and DEFAULT_MEM_LEVEL are internal. The static import of PerMessageDeflateDecoder.* brings in FRAME_TAIL and EMPTY_DEFLATE_BLOCK, which it inherits from DeflateDecoder; the C# using static names DeflateDecoder, the class that declares them. ZlibCodecFactory.newZlibEncoder(ZlibWrapper.NONE, level, windowSize, memLevel) creates codec-compression's JdkZlibEncoder on the BCL raw DeflateStream for windowSize 15 and memLevel 8, the values of every default configuration; any other window size or memory level needs jzlib, which is library-not-ported (owner decision 2026-11-23), so the factory throws NotSupportedException when the first frame is compressed, where the JVM without jzlib on the class path fails with NoClassDefFoundError (src/Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Compression/ZlibCodecFactory.cs). ZlibCodecFactory.isSupportingWindowSizeAndMemLevel() is false for the same reason, so the default handshakers behave as Java without jzlib (no window-size negotiation for the local deflater). EmbeddedChannel.builder().handlers(...).build() is new EmbeddedChannel.Builder().Handlers(...).Build(), readInbound()/readOutbound() are ReadInbound<ByteBuf>()/ReadOutbound<ByteBuf>(), ctx.alloc().compositeBuffer() is ctx.Alloc().CompositeBuffer(), addComponent(true, buf) is AddComponent(buf, true) (the Buffer port's parameter order), numComponents() is the NumComponents property and msg.getClass().getName() is GetType().FullName. handlerRemoved overrides the Transport member; encode is Encode with IList<object> @out. CodecException is codec-base's.

review.scope: Public sealed class implementing IWebSocketClientExtensionHandshaker; the static import of PerMessageDeflateServerExtensionHandshaker.* is a using static of that class (constants and ParseInt). The three @Deprecated constructors (), (int, boolean, int, boolean, boolean) and (int, boolean, int, boolean, boolean, WebSocketExtensionFilterProvider) name their replacements and are not ported (owner decision 2026-11-16); their Javadocs are recorded below. ZlibCodecFactory.isSupportingWindowSizeAndMemLevel() is false because jzlib is library-not-ported, so the default configuration does not offer client_max_window_bits, as Java without jzlib; a negotiated client window below 15 makes the encoder fail at the first compressed frame (see DeflateEncoder). Integer.parseInt is the internal ParseInt (declared in PerMessageDeflateServerExtensionHandshaker, which the client handshaker statically imports): Java accepts an optional ASCII sign and decimal digits and throws NumberFormatException for null, for non-digits and for values outside the int range (https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/lang/Integer.html), and int.TryParse with NumberStyles.AllowLeadingSign and the invariant culture fails for null, non-digits and values outside the Int32 range (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.int32.tryparse?view=net-10.0), where ParseInt throws FormatException (the counterpart of NumberFormatException) with the messages of OpenJDK 17 ("Cannot parse null string", "For input string: \"...\"", https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openjdk/jdk17u/jdk-17+35/src/java.base/share/classes/java/lang/Integer.java, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openjdk/jdk17u/jdk-17+35/src/java.base/share/classes/java/lang/NumberFormatException.java); Java also accepts non-ASCII Unicode decimal digits (Character.digit), which the BCL rejects. Integer.toString is ToString with the invariant culture. HashMap<String, String> is Dictionary<string, string>: neither defines an iteration order ("no guarantees as to the order of the map", https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/util/HashMap.html; "The order in which the items are returned is undefined", https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.collections.generic.dictionary-2?view=net-10.0) and both allow null values, so the order of the negotiated parameters in the header may differ from Java's (RFC 7692 parameters are order-independent). The Iterator over parameters().entrySet() is an IEnumerator<KeyValuePair<string, string>>, and equalsIgnoreCase is string.Equals with StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.stringcomparison?view=net-10.0), the same for these ASCII parameter names. The inner (non-static) class PermessageDeflateExtension reads compressionLevel of its enclosing instance ("An instance i of a direct inner class C ... is associated with an instance of O, known as the immediately enclosing instance of i", https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se17/html/jls-8.html#jls-8.1.3); a C# nested class has no enclosing instance, so the handshaker is passed to its constructor as the first argument (field outer). IllegalArgumentException is ArgumentException with the numbers in the invariant culture; checkPositiveOrZero/checkNotNull are the Common ObjectUtil checks.

The package-private class and its constructors are internal; acceptInboundMessage overrides AcceptInboundMessage and decode overrides Decode. IllegalStateException is InvalidOperationException; thrown from AcceptInboundMessage, it is wrapped in a DecoderException by MessageToMessageDecoder.ChannelRead, as in Java (the test checks DecoderException). WebSocketExtension.RSV1 is IWebSocketExtension.RSV1.

The package-private class and its constructors are internal; acceptOutboundMessage overrides AcceptOutboundMessage and encode overrides Encode. IllegalStateException is InvalidOperationException; thrown from AcceptOutboundMessage, it is wrapped in an EncoderException by MessageToMessageEncoder.WriteAsync, as in Java (the test checks EncoderException). java.util.zip.Inflater is codec-compression's internal stand-in Inflater (InternalsVisibleTo; owner decisions 2026-11-23 and 2026-11-24), whose needsDictionary()/setDictionary() follow java.util.zip on the BCL streams. It is created as new Inflater(false, true) (exactRemaining): every SPDY stream sets FDICT, after which the stand-in reads one byte per Read and getRemaining() is exact anyway; exactRemaining also makes getRemaining() exact for a stream without FDICT, so a complete zlib stream followed by more bytes is an invalid header block as in Java (fed whole buffers, the bytes after the end would count as consumed). DataFormatException is the InvalidDataException of the stand-in and setDictionary's IllegalArgumentException is ArgumentException. The Buffer port has no hasArray()/array()/arrayOffset(); the private TryGetArray/ArrayOf of codec-compression's JdkZlibDecoder (AsReadOnlySequence and MemoryMarshal.TryGetArray, docs/buffer-porting.md, Array extraction) replace them. The package-private final class is internal sealed; end() is public in Java but keeps the internal accessibility of the overridden SpdyHeaderBlockDecoder.end(). The number in the exception text uses the invariant culture.

java.util.zip.Deflater is codec-compression's internal stand-in Deflater (InternalsVisibleTo; owner decisions 2026-11-23 and 2026-11-24): setDictionary(SPDY_DICT) writes the zlib header with FDICT and the dictionary's Adler-32 and keeps the dictionary as history; deflate(..., SYNC_FLUSH) is the stream's sync flush. The compressed bytes can differ from Java's zlib (.NET uses zlib-ng); the format and the inflated data are the same (the compression agent checked the SPDY encoder loop against CPython's zlib). The Buffer port has no hasArray()/array()/arrayOffset(); private TryGetArray/ArrayOf helpers replace them, as in JdkZlibEncoder. The protected constructors are protected internal (SpdyHttpCodec and the tests use them); putMessage/getMessage/removeMessage are protected virtual. catch (Throwable) is catch (Exception) and the writeAndFlush futures are discarded Tasks. setInt(PRIORITY, priority()) widens the CLR byte, the same value 0-7 as the Java byte. MessageToMessageEncoder<HttpObject> is the codec-base MessageToMessageEncoder<IHttpObject> with a typeof(...) matcher. headers.getInt(name) returns int? (Integer); unboxing it into an int is .Value, which throws InvalidOperationException for a missing header where Java's unboxing throws NullPointerException (both leave encode). (byte) getInt(PRIORITY, 0) is an unchecked narrowing to the CLR byte (the same low eight bits), and setPriority rejects a value above 7 as Java rejects one outside 0-7. The String values of the request line, the String headers get(...) results and "https" are wrapped in the Common StringCharSequence (a private Of keeps null); "Keep-Alive"/"Proxy-Connection" use the core HttpHeaders.Remove(string) overload. The codec-base IIterator<IEntry<ICharSequence, ICharSequence>> of iteratorCharSequence() keeps the hasNext()/next() loop, and AsciiString.of(...).toLowerCase() is AsciiString.Of(...).ToLowerCase(). The @SuppressWarnings lines have no counterpart.
The final classes with private constructors (SpdyHttpHeaders and the nested Names) are static classes of static readonly AsciiString constants (AsciiString.Cached).

MessageToMessageCodec<Object, HttpMessage> is the codec-base MessageToMessageCodec<object, IHttpMessage> with typeof(...) matchers. The ArrayDeque<Integer> is a LinkedList<int>, because remove(Object) removes the first occurrence of a stream id from the middle of the queue (LinkedList.Remove(T) removes the first occurrence); poll() returns the head or null (a private Poll()). ArrayDeque prohibits null elements (NullPointerException), so adding a null getInt(...) result throws ArgumentNullException (the checkNotNull mapping). NO_ID is a const.

Throwable is Exception; serialVersionUID has no counterpart. The cause-only constructor keeps Java's detail message cause.toString() through Common's ThrowableUtil.ThrowableToString (before 2026-11-24 a copy of the expression of codec-base's internal CodecException.ThrowableToString). newStatic is internal (package-private) and stores the origin frame with Common ThrowableUtil.UnknownStackTrace; the private shared constructor super(message, null, false, true) is base(message) with Debug.Assert(shared), because the CLR Exception has no suppression/writable-stack-trace switches; a null message gives the CLR default message where Java's getMessage() returns null (only SpdySessionHandler.PROTOCOL_EXCEPTION has one, and nothing reads it). StacklessSpdyProtocolException cannot override fillInStackTrace(); it freezes the first stack trace, as Common GlobalEventExecutor's StacklessUnsupportedOperationException does.

The Java interface takes the I prefix (owner rule); its methods stay methods. status()/setStatus are Status()/SetStatus. The package-private final class is internal sealed. AtomicInteger is an int field updated with Interlocked (Increment/Decrement/Add, whose result is the new value as addAndGet; Volatile.Read for get()). ConcurrentHashMap<Integer, StreamState> is ConcurrentDictionary<int, StreamState> (put is AddOrUpdate capturing the previous value, remove is TryRemove, get is TryGetValue through a private Get), and ConcurrentLinkedQueue is ConcurrentQueue (offer/peek/poll are Enqueue/TryPeek/TryDequeue). activeStreams() builds a SortedDictionary<int, StreamState> with the StreamComparator (an IComparer<int> holding the session, as the Java inner class reads activeStreams); it is returned as IDictionary<int, StreamState>, so StreamState is internal instead of private (a private nested type cannot appear in an internal signature). The local state of the SPDY_SESSION_STREAM_ID branch of getPendingWrite is renamed stream (C# local scopes, CS0136). ChannelPromise is the TaskCompletionSource whose Task SpdySessionHandler returned for the queued write, and setFailure is TrySetException, as ChunkedWriteHandler's PendingWrite fails its promise. The Java byte members (priority, flags) are CLR bytes, the octets on the wire, as the other codec ports map Java byte members (codec-haproxy, codec-mqtt and codec-memcache ByteValue()/Opcode()).

ChannelDuplexHandler is the Transport ChannelDuplexHandler; write/close are WriteAsync/CloseAsync whose Task replaces the promise (docs/codec-base-porting.md, Outbound operations). The handler completes, stores and listens to its write promises, so each ChannelPromise is a TaskCompletionSource (RunContinuationsAsynchronously, as ChunkedWriteHandler's queued writes) whose Task WriteAsync/CloseAsync return: ctx.write(msg, promise)/ctx.writeAndFlush(msg, promise)/ctx.close(promise) are private Write/WriteAndFlush/Close helpers that complete the promise from the context operation's Task with TrySetFromTask (the PromiseNotifier mapping of docs/common-task-composition.md), promise.setFailure is SetException, ctx.newPromise() a new TaskCompletionSource and ctx.newSucceededFuture() Task.CompletedTask. ChannelFuture.addListener is a continuation on Common's CLR-only EventExecutorTaskScheduler over ctx.Executor (owner decision 2026-11-24; handler's IdleStateHandler and core HttpServerKeepAliveHandler use it too): Java notifies a listener at once when the promise completes on its event loop, while a continuation on TaskScheduler.Default would run later on a thread-pool thread (docs/handler-porting.md, Listener timing). ClosingChannelFutureListener keeps its name with OperationComplete(Task). A queued data frame is written later without the caller's CancellationToken. AtomicInteger pings is an int with Interlocked, volatile int is a volatile field; IllegalArgumentException is ArgumentException. notApplicableMethods.reason: Zstandard comes from zstd-jni (com.github.luben.zstd, a JNI binding). System.IO.Compression gains ZstandardStream/ZstandardEncoder/ZstandardDecoder only in .NET 11 (its API page lists net-11.0 only), and the owner kept the solution on .NET 10 and decided on 2026-11-23 not to port the Zstd family (docs/codec-compression-porting.md), so Zstd, ZstdOptions, ZstdEncoder and ZstdDecoder have no C# type. The test builds an HttpContentCompressor with StandardCompressionOptions.zstd() and checks the zstd Content-Encoding choices, which need the not-ported ZstdOptions.
notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: determineEncoding picks "zstd" for Accept-Encoding values that prefer zstd when the compressor was configured with gzip, deflate, brotli, zstd and snappy options.

EmbeddedChannel readInbound()/readOutbound() are ReadInbound<T>()/ReadOutbound<T>(), content() is Content and refCnt() is RefCnt (docs/transport-porting.md). CharsetUtil.US_ASCII/UTF_8 are Encoding.ASCII/Encoding.UTF8 and String.getBytes() (the default charset) is Encoding.Default (docs/codec-smtp-porting.md; the bytes are ASCII). Anonymous handler/encoder/decoder classes are named nested classes. brotli4j is not ported; Brotli.IsAvailable() is always true (the BCL BrotliEncoder/BrotliDecoder, docs/codec-compression-porting.md), so the brotli conditions (@EnabledIf/@DisabledIf/assumptions) always let the tests run. The protected determineWrapper(String)/determineEncoding(String), which the Java tests call through package access, are reached through the nested TestCompressor; the [Obsolete] constructors and DetermineWrapper are used as in Java (CS0612/CS0618 are suppressed in the file), and the returned null wrapper is ZlibWrapper?. ByteBufUtil.hexDump is ByteBufUtil.HexDump; the gzip and brotli bytes produced by the codec-compression encoders match the Java hex expectations and lengths. brotli4j's DirectDecompress (a test-only cross-check) is the BCL System.IO.Compression.BrotliDecoder.Decompress, whose OperationStatus.Done means "source was successfully and completely decompressed into destination" (Java's DecoderJNI.Status.DONE). testExecutorPreserveOrdering uses the Transport ports (MultiThreadIoEventLoopGroup with LocalIoHandler, LocalServerChannel/LocalChannel, ServerBootstrap/Bootstrap) and is async: sync() is awaiting the Task, the ChannelInitializer<LocalChannel> and adapter subclasses are named nested classes, BlockingQueue.poll(1, SECONDS) is BlockingCollection.TryTake with a one-second timeout, and the @Deprecated pipeline.addLast(EventExecutorGroup, ChannelHandler...) (not ported, docs/transport-porting.md) is AddLast(group, null, handler), whose null name is generated as in Java. UUID.randomUUID() is Guid.NewGuid(). AssembledHttpResponse implements IHttpContent with the narrowed retain/touch and explicit IByteBufHolder/IReferenceCounted members (as DefaultHttpContent). CompositeByteBuf.addComponent(true, buf) is AddComponent(buf, true), the Buffer port's parameter order. UnsupportedOperationException is NotSupportedException and IllegalStateException InvalidOperationException.
