notApplicableMethods.reason: Zstandard comes from zstd-jni (com.github.luben.zstd, a JNI binding). System.IO.Compression gains ZstandardStream/ZstandardEncoder/ZstandardDecoder only in .NET 11 (its API page lists net-11.0 only), and the owner kept the solution on .NET 10 and decided on 2026-11-23 not to port the Zstd family (docs/codec-compression-porting.md), so Zstd, ZstdOptions, ZstdEncoder and ZstdDecoder have no C# type. HttpContentDecompressor passes a "zstd" Content-Encoding through undecoded, as Java does when Zstd.isAvailable() is false, so the zstd body cannot be decompressed.
notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: An aggregated response with "Content-Encoding: zstd" (SAMPLE_ZSTD_BYTES) is decompressed to SAMPLE_STRING and the Content-Encoding header is removed.

A Java String passed as a CharSequence is a StringCharSequence (a C# string is not an ICharSequence) and the CharSequence results are compared as strings.

The old algorithm returns the rejection instead of throwing a preallocated stack-less exception that the loop catches: a CLR throw "can be orders of magnitude slower" (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/design-guidelines/exceptions-and-performance). The same 2^32 values are walked in 256 slices of 2^24 values on Parallel.For (one array/AsciiString/view per slice), because the sequential walk did not finish within 10 minutes on this host; @DisabledForJreRange has no counterpart, the failure message is built only for a failing assertion.
As headerValueValidationMustRejectAllValuesRejectedByOldAlgorithm: the old name algorithm returns the rejection, and the 2^32 values are walked in 256 Parallel.For slices.

caseMappings.adaptation: JUnit 5 tests become xUnit v3 tests with the same names (first letter upper case); package-private @Test methods are public [Fact]s and @ParameterizedTest @ValueSource(strings) is a [Theory] with one [InlineData] per value (the display-name pattern of @ParameterizedTest(name = ...) has no xUnit counterpart). EmbeddedChannel is the Transport EmbeddedChannel (readInbound()/readOutbound() are ReadInbound<T>()/ReadOutbound<T>()); HttpRequest, HttpResponse, HttpMessage, HttpContent and LastHttpContent are the I-prefixed interfaces and content() is the Content property. CharsetUtil.US_ASCII/UTF_8 are Encoding.ASCII/Encoding.UTF8 (docs/codec-smtp-porting.md). IllegalArgumentException is ArgumentException and NumberFormatException is FormatException (docs/codec-base-porting.md; the decoder throws FormatException where Java throws NumberFormatException), so assertInstanceOf and AssertJ isInstanceOf are Assert.IsAssignableFrom<T>, hasMessageContaining is Assert.Contains on Message, and asserts with a message use XunitAssertMessages.AssertM. Java passes Strings as CharSequence header names (HttpHeadersTestUtils.of); a C# string is not an ICharSequence, so they are wrapped in StringCharSequence by HttpHeadersTestUtils.Of. DecoderResult is the codec-base type. EmbeddedChannel is the Transport EmbeddedChannel (readInbound()/readOutbound() are ReadInbound<T>()/ReadOutbound<T>()); HttpRequest, HttpResponse, HttpMessage, HttpContent and LastHttpContent are the I-prefixed interfaces and content() is the Content property. CharsetUtil.US_ASCII/UTF_8 are Encoding.ASCII/Encoding.UTF8 (docs/codec-smtp-porting.md). IllegalArgumentException is ArgumentException and NumberFormatException is FormatException (docs/codec-base-porting.md; the decoder throws FormatException where Java throws NumberFormatException), so assertInstanceOf and AssertJ isInstanceOf are Assert.IsAssignableFrom<T>, hasMessageContaining is Assert.Contains on Message, and asserts with a message use XunitAssertMessages.AssertM. Java passes Strings as CharSequence header names (HttpHeadersTestUtils.of); a C# string is not an ICharSequence, so they are wrapped in StringCharSequence by HttpHeadersTestUtils.Of. AsciiString.contentEqualsIgnoreCase(String, String) wraps both values with Of(...). The anonymous ChannelInboundHandlerAdapter of reentrantClose is the named nested ReentrantCloseHandler and ctx.close() is ctx.CloseAsync(). new Exception(cause) keeps the cause as InnerException, printStackTrace() writes the exception to Console.Error, Integer.toHexString is ToString("x", invariant culture) and Arrays.fill is Array.Fill. In testDecodeWholeRequestInMultipleSteps the LastHttpContent local is renamed from c to last, because the loop variable c of the same method would clash with it in C# (CS0136). All 78 declared methods (108 test cases with the theory rows) pass; the tests run on the core HttpObjectDecoder/HttpRequestDecoder without changes.

notApplicableMethods.reason: An InetSocketAddress built from InetAddress.getByName("localhost") keeps the host name for getHostString(); the CLR counterpart of a resolved address, IPEndPoint, keeps only the IPAddress, and NetUtil.GetHostname returns the numeric IPEndPoint address without a DNS lookup, so no CLR endpoint is both resolved and named. The unresolved DnsEndPoint case is testFormatHostnameForHttpFromUnesolvedAddressWithHostname.
notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: formatHostnameForHttp of a resolved InetSocketAddress created from a host name returns that host name ("localhost").

StandardCharsets.UTF_16 is Encoding.BigEndianUnicode. The JDK UTF-16 charset writes a big-endian byte-order mark when encoding (https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/nio/charset/Charset.html), so Java expects "%FE%FF%00%A5"; .NET Encoding.GetBytes never writes the preamble (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.text.encoding.getpreamble?view=net-10.0), so the C# expectation is "%00%A5", the same big-endian code unit without the mark.

Java's peerEchoWrite is the promise that the protocol handler created for the peer's close frame and passed down the pipeline, so the stalled handler saw that very promise. The Transport passes no promise down (each handler returns its own Task, docs/transport-porting.md: promise arguments are the returned Task), so the stalled handler's TaskCompletionSource is not the cascaded promise: the C# test checks the two stalled writes, the close and the application's close Task, but cannot observe the cascaded promise, so assertTrue(peerEchoWrite.isDone()) has no counterpart (the cascade itself runs in WebSocketProtocolHandler.CloseSent).
